assumptions.scope: symbolic forcing/observable dictionary; no data fitting

rows.frequency_source: single eccentric orbit gives n and 2n through O(e^2)
rows.missing_assumption: nonzero e, p, p+3, beta, tau_chi, and Lambda
rows.notes: This supplies the first concrete F(Y(t)) template without using data or clock-sector assumptions.
rows.observable_projection: linear channel O_hat = Lambda G F_hat

rows.forcing_class: any known harmonic drive F_k cos(Omega_k t)
rows.frequency_source: one or more known drive frequencies
rows.missing_assumption: projection must not be arbitrary per frequency
rows.notes: If Lambda is common, O_hat/(Lambda F_hat) recovers G. If Lambda is a finite polynomial nuisance, raise the comparator order accordingly.
rows.observable_projection: known nonzero Lambda or finite-dimensional Lambda(Omega)
rows.verdict: preserves the pole relation after calibration

rows.forcing_class: same drive construction across several systems
rows.missing_assumption: common tau_chi or independently specified body-dependence
rows.notes: Without shared parameters, each system can be fit by its own effective derivative coefficients.
rows.verdict: usable only with shared tau_chi relation

rows.forcing_class: F = F1 cos(Omega1 t) + F2 cos(Omega2 t)
rows.frequency_source: two known distinct drives in one system
rows.missing_assumption: known distinct drives and nonzero projection
rows.notes: Enough to beat real degree-1 or degree-2 derivative EFTs, not arbitrary higher finite order.
rows.observable_projection: linear channel O_hat = Lambda G F_hat
rows.verdict: two transfer samples but no sidebands

rows.notes: An arbitrary frequency-local projection nuisance can absorb the pole relation.

rows.frequency_source: e=0, p=0, or p=-3 at O(e^2)
rows.missing_assumption: nonzero harmonic content in selected invariant
rows.notes: No eccentric modulation, no first harmonic, or no second harmonic at this order removes the two-point test.
